fields.summary: Find users by their complete e-mail address in the user search

content.text: The user search only looks at usernames and names. Administrators often know a person only by e-mail address and cannot find the account. The search should also find a user by e-mail address, but only by the complete address: it must not be possible to discover other people's addresses by trying parts of them.
The same search is behind the user list (Users management, search box) and the "Name" field used to add a member on a project's Permissions page.

The examples below assume two users created by the administrator in addition to admin: username jdoe, name John Doe, e-mail John.Doe@example.com; and username msmith, name Mary Smith, e-mail mary@example.com.

In the user list, searching for a user's complete e-mail address finds that user, although the address is not part of the username or the name: "John.Doe@example.com" lists John Doe only, "mary@example.com" lists Mary Smith only, and the page title reads "Users (1)".
Upper and lower case make no difference for the address: "john.doe@example.com" finds John Doe and "MARY@example.com" finds Mary Smith.
Only a complete address matches. Searching for "@example.com", "mary@", "example.com" or "%@example.com" finds no user: the list shows "No users found." and the page title reads "Users (0)".
Searching by username and name works as before, on any part of either and regardless of case: "jd" finds John Doe, "SMITH" and "mary" find Mary Smith, "nobody" finds no user.
An empty search lists all users: admin, John Doe and Mary Smith, with the title "Users (3)".

On a project's Permissions page, typing the complete address "mary@example.com" in the "Name" field suggests "Mary Smith (msmith)"; typing "mary@" or "@example.com" suggests nobody; "smi" still suggests "Mary Smith (msmith)". A suggestion shows the name and the username, never the e-mail address.
The user list and its search remain for administrators only: a signed-in user who is not an administrator gets "Access Forbidden" (403) on both.
No change to how e-mail addresses are entered, validated or displayed.
